newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thousands demonstrate over Renault plant closure.
newsitem.headline: Thousands demonstrate over Renault plant closure.

text.p: Thousands of French car workers protested outside the headquarters of Renault on Tuesday ahead of a joint demonstration with their Belgian counterparts over the French carmaker's plans to close a factory in Belgium.

Trade unions are predicting that about 10,000 will take part in the rally outside Renault's offices on the outskirts of Paris when a convoy of 80 coaches arrives with some 3,000 workers from the doomed Belgian plant.

"The bigger the mobilisation, the greater the pressure will be on (Renault chairman Louis) Schweitzer to retreat," Philippe Martinez, head of the Communist-led CGT union, said outside the car manufacturer's Boulogne-Billancourt headquarters.

The French contingent was joined by 50 workers from Renault plants in Spain for a protest which headed on a march along the Paris ring-road and was due to return to the Boulogne-Billancourt offices, where Schweitzer was to meet staff representatives at 1300 GMT.

The closure of the Vilvoorde plant near Brussels with 3,100 job losses has provoked a storm of controversy among unions and politicians in both countries, both for its severity and the sudden way in which it was announced on February 27.
Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene has condemned the decision and the French government and President Jacques Chirac have criticised Renault for the way it handled the closure.
"I do not approve. I believe there has to be a minimum of form and this has to be respected," Chirac said during a television interview on Monday night.
Renault, confronted with weak demand and cutthroat price competition in the European car market, plans to shut the Belgian factory and cut another 2,764 jobs in France in an attempt to restructure.
Another trade union spokesman said the protestors would try to get the Belgian closure reconsidered and take advantage of French job promotion laws to protect jobs via a cut in working hours.

"We're going to ask for two things at the meeting -- that Renault reconsider the closure of the Vilvoorde plant, and for the start of negotiations to reduce working hours to preserve jobs under the (French) Robien law," Emmanuel Couvreur, a spokesman for the French CFDT union, said.
